consignes: Le test s'adapte à tes réponses : il commence au niveau B1, puis monte ou descend selon tes résultats, par séries de six questions (grammaire, vocabulaire, lecture et écoute). Compte 12 à 30 questions, 10 à 20 minutes. Tu ne verras pas la correction pendant le test. Si tu ne connais pas la réponse, clique sur « Je ne sais pas » : répondre au hasard fausserait le résultat.

niveaux.description: Tu comprends et utilises des phrases très simples : te présenter, parler de ta famille, commander, demander ton chemin.
Tu te débrouilles au quotidien : raconter ton week-end au passé, faire des achats, parler de ton travail et de projets simples.
Tu tiens une conversation sur des sujets familiers : donner ton avis, raconter une expérience, te débrouiller en voyage ou en entretien.
Tu discutes avec aisance : argumenter, nuancer, comprendre l'essentiel d'articles, de séries et de réunions de travail.
Tu t'exprimes avec précision et naturel, même sur des sujets complexes, et tu saisis les sous-entendus.

*Why do many companies now use a mixed system?*
choix: To balance productivity and team communication
Because employees refuse to work from home
Because offices have become too expensive
To reduce the number of managers
questions.texte: Remote work has become common since 2020. Many employees say they are more productive at home, but some managers worry that teams communicate less. As a result, many companies now ask staff to come to the office two or three days a week.

*What does the research suggest?*
choix: The effects depend on the teenager's existing friendships.
Social media isolates all teenagers in the same way.
Social media has no effect on friendships.
Isolated teenagers benefit the most from social media.
questions.texte: Critics of social media often argue that it isolates people. Yet recent research paints a more nuanced picture: for teenagers who already have strong friendships offline, online platforms tend to reinforce those relationships, whereas isolated teenagers are more likely to experience negative effects.

questions.texte: The council's decision to close the library has sparked outrage among residents, who claim it was taken without proper consultation. Officials, however, insist that a public survey was carried out last spring.

*What is the sceptics' main objection?*
choix: The results may not apply to every sector.
Staff were less happy during the trials.
questions.texte: Proponents of the four-day week point to pilot schemes in which productivity held steady while staff wellbeing improved. Sceptics counter that such trials have largely involved office-based firms whose output is hard to measure, and that the results may not translate to sectors such as healthcare or manufacturing.

questions.texte: While the technology undoubtedly streamlines routine tasks, the report cautions against assuming it will cut costs across the board: implementation, training and maintenance can easily offset the initial savings.

questions.texte: Far from being a sign of indecision, the minister's willingness to revise the plan in light of new evidence should be seen as a strength.

questions.ecoute: Had I known how much paperwork was involved, I'd probably have thought twice. That said, I don't regret it for a second.

questions.ecoute: What struck me most wasn't the size of the city, but how quiet it was at night, which is the last thing you'd expect from a capital.
